messages:
maria: rolled nv driver 535.102 -> 537.12 across east3 this morning. noticing MIG profiles missing on ~12/120 nodes. GPUs report different UUIDs than inventory. example `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_uuid,name,mig.mode.current --format=csv` output attached.

infra-bot: deploy-job #build/driver-upgrade completed 2026-02-18T09:23Z :white_check_mark:

sandeep: saw batch jobs failing with "no suitable device" in k8s pods, kubelet logs show device plugin couldn't match UUIDs :warning:

anya: can we try `sudo nvidia-smi mig -e`? last time re-enabling MIG on the node fixed profile listing.

leo: don't re-enable blindly — we had persistent state mismatch when the driver migration changed devicenode ids. Need to run `nvidia-smi -L` and compare against inventory mapping in /etc/gpu-inventory.json

maria: attaching snippet:
```
# nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-abc123)
GPU 1: A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-def456)
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_uuid,name,mig.mode.current --format=csv
GPU-abc123, A100-SXM4-80GB, Disabled
GPU-def456, A100-SXM4-80GB, Disabled
```

ops-oncall: triage plan: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) run `gpu-inventory sync --force` which reconciles UUID->devicenode mapping, 3) reapply MIG configs with `migctl apply --from /srv/mig-profiles/{cluster}.yaml`, 4) if failure, rollback driver to 535.102. I'll start a canary on 3 nodes.

sandeep: +1 to canary. also open a ticket with NVIDIA — seems like kernel->driver API changed ordering.

maria: canary started on 3 nodes (east3-canny-1..3). I'll post results. Thanks :thumbsup:
